title: Section 1033 open banking rule: final revised rule by end of 2027

strapi.title: Section 1033 into law by end of 2027

needs_input: The idea text is empty, so the editor has not stated the outcome being tracked. Please write the outcome in one sentence.

Section 1033 is already law: it was enacted in the Dodd-Frank Act in 2010. 'Into law' therefore has to mean one of: (a) a CFPB final rule implementing or revising Section 1033 (currently 12 CFR part 1033), published in the Federal Register; (b) a federal statute enacted by Congress that amends Section 1033; or (c) a state open-banking law, such as New York's pending bills. Choose one. The draft below assumes (a).
Confirm whether a proposed rule (NPRM) counts. The draft assumes it does not; only a final rule counts.
Confirm whether an interim final rule counts as a 'final rule'. The CFPB has been reported as considering that route.
Confirm the deadline. The draft assumes 'end of 2027' means December 31, 2027.
Confirm whether a court vacating the 2024 rule, or lifting the injunction, should change the answer. The draft treats neither as sufficient on its own.
Confirm the resolution date basis: Federal Register publication date (drafted) or the date the rule takes effect.
question: Will the CFPB publish a final rule amending or replacing the Personal Financial Data Rights rule (12 CFR part 1033, implementing Section 1033 of the Dodd-Frank Act) in the Federal Register on or before December 31, 2027?

resolution.yes: A final rule amending, replacing, or re-issuing 12 CFR part 1033 (the Personal Financial Data Rights rule) appears in the Federal Register with a publication date on or before 2027-12-31. An interim final rule counts only if the editor confirms it does.
resolution.no: No such final rule is published in the Federal Register by 2027-12-31. A proposed rule, a court ruling, or a statute alone does not count.
resolution.source: Federal Register (federalregister.gov), searching for 12 CFR part 1033 and CFPB final rules; cross-checked against the CFPB Personal Financial Data Rights page and reginfo.gov.

base_rate.reasoning: As of 2026-11-15, the CFPB has not published a proposed rule. Its revised proposal (titled 'Personal Financial Data Rights Reconsideration') was sent to OIRA for review in early August 2026, and the CFPB's August 2025 advance notice was the first step. For a final rule by 2027-12-31, the NPRM would need to publish around December 2026, followed by a 60 to 90 day comment period and a final rule within roughly 9 to 12 months. Comparable case: the 2023 proposal (October 19, 2023) led to the 2024 final rule (October 22, 2024), about 12 months. That timeline only just fits. Against it: the rule is enjoined pending reconsideration, so urgency is lower. The CFPB's funding and staffing have been disputed in court through 2026. Speed is not assured. A Dec 2026 publication with a fast comment period could still meet the deadline, which is why the draft sits at about 15% rather than lower. Caveat: several secondary sources (blogs) predict a Q4 2026 NPRM, but these are not primary and were not verified against the Federal Register.

signals.label: OIRA clears the revised NPRM (raises: publication likely within weeks)
NPRM published in the Federal Register, starting the comment clock (raises)
NPRM comment period closes without a major new delay (raises slightly)
Final rule submitted to OIRA review (decisive procedural step; publication typically follows within weeks)
CFPB issues an interim final rule instead of the NPRM-to-final route (raises a 'final' rule but changes the process; confirm counting rule)
Court lifts or modifies the Eastern District of Kentucky injunction, or dismisses Forcht Bank v. CFPB (raises: reduces pressure to finish)
Final judgment vacating the 2024 rule (ambiguous: may prompt a replacement rule or reduce urgency)
Permanent CFPB director confirmed, or acting-director authority lapses (direction depends on nominee's priorities)
New court order, funding shortfall, or staff reduction constrains CFPB rulemaking capacity (lowers)
Unified Agenda lists a final-rule date on or before 2027-12-31 (raises modestly; agendas often slip)
Congress enacts an amendment to Section 1033 itself (only relevant if the editor chooses the statute reading; decisive for that reading)
A federal bill touching open banking or 1033 (e.g., GLBA modernization) passes a chamber (small effect on the rule question)
New York bills A10640/S9483 or similar state law enacted (not federal; affects only the state reading)

actors.name: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB)
actors.role: Issuing agency. Reconsidering the 2024 rule and drafting the revised NPRM. Only body that can issue the implementing rule.

actors.name: Russ Vought (acting CFPB director; OMB director)
actors.role: Leads the CFPB's reconsideration. Acting tenure has been disputed under the Vacancies Act. Also controls OMB, which runs the OIRA review.

actors.name: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA, within OMB)
actors.role: Gatekeeper for the NPRM and final rule under Executive Order 12866. Review timing controls publication timing.

actors.name: E.D. Kentucky federal court (Forcht Bank, N.A. v. CFPB)
actors.role: Entered the October 2025 order barring CFPB enforcement until reconsideration is complete. Its rulings on the injunction or the merits affect timing and the status of the 2024 rule.

actors.name: Forcht Bank and bank trade groups (ABA, CBA)
actors.role: Plaintiffs who challenged the 2024 rule. They want fee allowances and major revisions, and have pressed the CFPB to suspend compliance dates.

actors.name: Financial Technology Association and fintech/data-aggregator interests (incl. FDX)
actors.role: Intervened to defend the 2024 rule. Oppose the fee and access rollbacks under reconsideration. FDX was recognized as the standard-setter in 2025.

actors.name: Senate Banking and House Financial Services Committees
actors.role: Oversight of the CFPB; could legislate on Section 1033 or related privacy and open-banking provisions (e.g., GLBA modernization bill).

actors.name: Federal Reserve Board (funding channel)
actors.role: CFPB funding flows through the Fed. Funding disputes in 2026 affect CFPB capacity to finish rulemaking.

actors.name: New York State Legislature (Assembly A10640 / Senate S9483)
actors.role: Introduced state-level open-banking data-sharing bills in March 2026. Would create state rights regardless of the federal outcome.
